extracted.intended_audience: congressional committee members, congressional staff, journalists, and the public following the Volkswagen emissions investigation
extracted.subtask_description: Transcript of a congressional oversight hearing (questions-and-answers) with Volkswagen leadership about the emissions ('defeat device') scandal, corporate response, investigations, and remedies for affected customers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notify affected customers
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide direct notification to owners (e.g., letter stating status and requested actions). Example text cited: "Your vehicle remains both safe to drive and legal to drive. You do not need to take any action at this time. All we ask is for your patience."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification should be clear and specific; committee members criticized a vague request for 'patience' as insufficient. Use multiple channels (mail, dealers, website) and ensure customers can determine whether their vehicle is affected without technical disassembly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide clear timeline for fixes and scenarios
rubrics_metrics.description: Tell customers expected timelines for technical fixes and distinguish best-case and worst-case scenarios. On record: Generation 3 ('15/'16) — "beginning of next year a complete fix"; Generation 2 — "won't start... before the middle of next year"; Generation 1 — no date but discussions with EPA/CARB forthcoming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish specific target dates or windows for each vehicle generation and state uncertainty clearly so customers understand how long vehicles may remain unfixed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain the technical nature of the defect (the 'defeat device')
rubrics_metrics.description: Give a plain-language technical explanation of what the defeat device is and how it works. Example from testimony: "the defeat device is not a device, but it's a software code... which detects whether a car is on the dyno testing environment or whether the car is on the road being driven."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include detection mechanisms (e.g., steering wheel angle changes used to detect dyno vs. road) and explain why detection was difficult (hidden in millions of lines of code).

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer remedies and compensation to customers
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider and communicate customer remedies such as buyback/repurchase at pre-notice fair market value, rebates for lost value, or other financial compensation. Testimony: discussion of allowing customers to return the car for what they paid; providing rebate for lost value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess and publicize remedy options, including buyback programs and value compensation; explain eligibility and process. Committee members urged buyback as a strong trust-restoring remedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider and enable loaner cars or dealer-provided interim relief
rubrics_metrics.description: Address immediate customer needs (loaner vehicles, transportation) and whether dealers will be compensated for providing loaners. Testimony: dealers were given discretionary funds to help customers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide and communicate whether loaners will be provided, how dealers are reimbursed, and any caps/eligibility; explicit policy is preferable to leaving it to dealer discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide dealers with discretionary funds and clear dealer policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Empower dealers to assist customers in significant cases via discretionary funds. Testimony: "we gave the dealers the discretionary funds which they could use at their discretion in order to help customers".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish guidance for dealers on how to use funds, examples of acceptable uses (loaners, immediate repairs/reimbursements), and escalation paths for large or systemic issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish an online VIN lookup and clearly classify affected vehicle generations
rubrics_metrics.description: Make it easy for consumers to know if their vehicle is affected (e.g., a website where entering VIN shows if affected and whether Generation 1/2/3). Testimony: suggestion to provide a VIN lookup because not everyone can identify engine type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a public VIN lookup tool and explicit mapping of VINs to generation/engine types so owners can quickly determine impact and expected remedy timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be transparent about internal and external investigations and share findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct and disclose results of internal audits and external investigations (e.g., Group Revision audit, law firm Jones Day probe) and share relevant documents with oversight bodies. Testimony: internal audit (Sep 22–29) and Jones Day were referenced; committee requested copies of preliminary findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commit to timely document production to oversight entities, summarize preliminary findings publicly where possible, and explain scope and limitations of investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperate fully with regulators and congressional committees
rubrics_metrics.description: Commit to providing information and cooperating with EPA, CARB, and congressional oversight. Testimony: repeated commitments to 'get as much information as possible to this committee' and to cooperate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide timely access to requested documents, make senior executives available for testimony, and engage constructively with regulators to resolve compliance issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose and explain disciplinary actions and personnel accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Inform stakeholders about suspensions, resignations, or prosecutions of responsible individuals while respecting legal/privacy constraints. Testimony: references to suspended employees (three reported) and resignations (e.g., Christian Klingler).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the scope of disciplinary actions, why names may be withheld (e.g., German law), and provide periodic updates on accountability measures and outcomes of investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accrue and disclose financial estimates for penalties and remediation
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate and report financial impacts, including accruals for expected fines and remediation costs. Testimony: "the company has accrued directly 6.5 billion euros in the first step in this year."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain basis for accruals, update estimates as investigations progress, and disclose categories (fines, recall fixes, customer compensation, legal costs).

rubrics_metrics.name: State safety and legal status of vehicles clearly
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify whether affected vehicles are safe and legal to drive. Testimony: company repeatedly relied on EPA's statement that "these vehicles are safe to drive."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide authoritative safety guidance and a clear legal status statement (e.g., per EPA/CARB determinations); explain any differences between safety and compliance remediation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage independent external experts and counsel
rubrics_metrics.description: Retain outside law firms and technical experts to investigate and quantify issues (e.g., Jones Day, technical experts). Testimony: documents were turned over to Jones Day; experts hired to work out remediation costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use independent third parties to increase credibility of findings and to assist in remediation planning; disclose the role and scope of external advisors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicate corporate responsibility, take ownership, and outline trust-restoration steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge failures, accept responsibility where appropriate, and outline steps to restore trust (e.g., aggressive compliance, making it right for customers, managing dealers/suppliers). Testimony: multiple members urged 'aggressively compliant and aggressively trying to make it right' and restoring faith in corporate structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish a remediation and governance plan (process improvements, oversight changes), timelines for implementation, and measurable milestones for rebuilding credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure technical fixes preserve fuel economy and engine performance
rubrics_metrics.description: When proposing software or hardware fixes, verify they address emissions while managing fuel economy and engine performance. Testimony: discussion whether the fix could manage fuel economy, engine performance, and emissions — Horn: 'I think it's a great question' and indicated fixes could handle these.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test and document that remedies do not unduly degrade vehicle performance or fuel economy; communicate expected performance post-fix to customers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make communications accessible and reach all affected customers
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not rely on technical knowledge of owners; provide accessible tools and clear instructions. Testimony: members stressed that owners cannot 'take apart the engine' and need simple ways to know if affected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use plain language, online VIN tools, direct mail, and dealer outreach so all owners — including used-car buyers — can determine impact and remedies.
